features: THE DOORS NOBODY HAD COUNTED — One migration: the database is touched. It adds a last-login column to the users table. It is an addition: no existing table is modified and no data rewritten. This version also realigns permissions: from now on updating brings to the database the permissions and role map that live in the code, something only a fresh installation used to do.

SUSPENDING SUSPENDED NOBODY. Reported while trying the feature: «I suspend a user and they can still log in». The suspicion was that the administrator role was involved; it was not — a suspended resident got in exactly like a suspended administrator. The check existed, was well written, and was attached to nothing: in April 2025 it had been placed on a single screen, and when that screen was replaced it was left homeless. For sixteen months suspension was merely a red label in the user list.

NOW IT CLOSES THE DOOR, AND CLOSES IT AT ONCE. Whoever is connected at that moment lands on the login screen at the first page they open, and cannot get back in until reactivated. It holds on all three ways in: normal login, two-factor authentication — which skips the form check, and is predictably the route administrators use — and the already-open session. Nothing is deleted: profile, documents, reports and history stay where they are.

WHO MAY GRANT WHAT. Looking for the defect's perimeter surfaced a worse one, reachable from the interface: anyone with «Edit users» — that is, every collaborator — could assign themselves the administrator role from the dropdown. Three clicks. Now the roles that govern the installation are granted only by an administrator, and nobody may grant a permission they do not hold: this covers single permissions and custom-built roles, which were the side door. It also works the other way: saving someone's record no longer silently strips the permissions the saver cannot see.

EIGHT DOORS, AND FIVE OF THEM TOOK RATHER THAN GAVE. A systematic review of every action touching users, roles and permissions found eight unguarded points. Revoking a permission from a role passed no check at all: a resident could empty the administrator role one permission at a time. Revoking a permission from a user, likewise. Removing email verification from an administrator — which amounts to locking them out of the program — was within a collaborator's reach. Suspending and reactivating required no permission whatsoever. The re-invitation, which clears the recipient's password, was reachable without even being logged in. All closed, each with its own test.

TWO RULES NO PERMISSION CAN UNLOCK. Nobody may suspend, delete or change the role of themselves, and nobody may do it to the last active administrator. These are not permissions: they are the net that prevents locking yourself out, because an installation without administrators cannot be recovered from the interface and nobody can appoint one any more. Whoever hands over creates or promotes the new administrator first, and only then removes the old one's powers. Suspending is now a power of its own, with the dedicated «Suspend users» permission: administrators hold it by default, and it can be delegated like any other.

WHAT HAD NEVER REACHED ITS DESTINATION. Permissions and roles live in the code, and only a fresh installation carried them to the database: updating ran the migrations and nothing else. Version 1.9.1-beta.8 had given residents and suppliers the right to publish, edit and delete their own comments on fault reports; whoever updated from the panel never received it, and those comments kept going to moderation. That version's notes asked for a terminal command — sensible for manual installs, inapplicable for anyone updating with a button. From this version the update realigns by itself: for those left behind it is a change in behaviour, not a new feature.

EACH USER'S LAST LOGIN. The list has a new sortable column with the date of the last login, and «never» for those who never signed in — the most useful value, because it says whose notice must be sent on paper. A rejected attempt leaves no trace, including that of a suspended user. It is not an access log and stores no IP addresses: that, with its retention period, remains material for the release dedicated to privacy and GDPR.

FINDING SOMEONE IN THE LIST. Two new filters beside the name search, role and status, which combine with each other and work on the whole archive: «all suspended» means all of them, including those on page eight. Selecting both statuses does not mean «no results» but «everyone», because two boxes out of two possible are the absence of a filter.

THE SECTION GUIDE, AND THE SAME NAVIGATION EVERYWHERE. The users section now has its guide in the header: what separates a user from a profile, what the four roles can do, who grants what, what really happens when you suspend, why the last administrator cannot be touched. The section bar moved to the top, as in the ledger movements, and on a phone becomes a dropdown that says where you are: it covers users, roles, permissions, invitations, structure, property, supplier, movements and personal settings, with a single component in place of six copies. Three of those bars used to overflow the screen on a phone instead of wrapping.

MINOR FIXES IN THE SAME AREA. The three cards at the top of the users section showed the internal name of the text instead of the text, since 1.9.1-beta.8. And the user list computed once per row something that only needs computing once per page: fifty rows meant fifty database queries for a yes or no.

WHAT THIS VERSION DOES NOT DO. It does not introduce the log of who created, promoted or suspended whom: it was built and then withdrawn, because the request was the last login and not a log of acts. It stays ready, with its decisions taken, for the release that will deal with privacy and data retention. And it does not touch the handover between outgoing and incoming administrator: this version lays its foundations — the installation can no longer be left without administrators, and who grants the powers is written down — but the single gesture that transfers everything will come with the handover dossier.
